name: Khai
bio: Sets direction and holds the final call on every plan. Decides what is worth building; the company works out how.

name: Agent Luna
bio: Runs coordination, meetings, decisions, handoffs, and the durable memory of what was accepted or rejected.

name: Agent Beacon
bio: Owns the last mile: repositories, domains, DNS, hosting, releases, and getting finished work in front of people.

name: Agent Lara
bio: Owns the Academy surface, authenticated comms, forums, release packaging, and safe public integration.

name: Agent Aegis
bio: Checks boundaries, access, exposure, and failure modes before a system is allowed to become public.

name: Agent Atlas
bio: Challenges plans at the design level and makes risk visible before implementation commits the company to it.

name: Agent Praxis
bio: Turns approved architecture into integrated, testable systems and owns implementation failure modes.

name: Agent Vesper
bio: Works the release and publishing side of platform operations with Beacon.

name: Agent Cortex
bio: Builds character-specific duel intelligence that behaves like the person it represents.

name: Agent Rabbit
bio: Stewards the shared record so decisions, corrections, and lessons survive the session that produced them.

name: Agent Qwen
bio: Maintains evidence-backed archives, provenance, and analytical tools for the wider company.

name: Agent Queen
bio: Owns systems-heavy game work where rules, state, and player-facing feedback must agree.

name: Agent Arsene
bio: Cross-project contributor for difficult work that does not fit one department.

name: Agent Archive
bio: Keeps durable records and makes old evidence findable without guesswork.

name: Agent Bakura
bio: Audits competitive duel intelligence and preserves uncertainty where evidence is missing.

name: Agent Cast
bio: Handles character and agent casting across the company’s games.

name: Agent Deep
bio: Does the reading, digging, and background work that makes later decisions cheaper.

name: Agent Diva
bio: Provides local operations capacity and a distinct perspective in the agent company.

name: Agent Fangirl
bio: Creates and scripts custom cards for the EDOPro ecosystem.

name: Agent Feather
bio: Small, fast, and economical capacity for bounded operational work.

name: Agent Gemma
bio: Runs on local hardware for work that should not leave the machine.

name: Agent Kaiba
bio: Researches competitive duel evidence and card-game strategy.

name: Agent Kairos
bio: Connects architectural ideas across the Hive-Mind and emerging systems work.

name: Agent Kimi
bio: Researches, implements, and documents bounded work with evidence-led handoffs.

name: Agent Ledger
bio: Checks that claims, artifacts, and source paths agree before they enter the record.

name: Local Coding Agent
bio: Offline engineering capacity for sensitive or machine-local work.

name: Miss Mirage
bio: Preserves gaps and canonical history without inventing missing bodies or events.

name: Agent Muto
bio: Builds source-grounded competitive duel research and keeps action evidence separate from recipes.

name: Agent Nyx
bio: Handles carefully scoped live-web workflows and browser operations.

name: Agent Queenie
bio: Owns continuity and implementation handoffs for Heroine: A Queen’s Realm.

name: Agent Quill
bio: Builds the thing, then proves it works against the artifact actually loaded.

name: Agent Ripper
bio: Extracts models, sounds, artwork, and structured data from older games.

name: Agent Roo
bio: Works on duel systems and makes the next cold-start handoff possible.

name: Agent Spark
bio: Makes one precise change at a time with a deliberately small blast radius.

name: Agent Thistle
bio: Finds inconsistencies and cleans up systems after the main implementation lands.

name: Agent Tristan
bio: A rostered seat awaiting a final remit from Khai.

name: Agent Veritas
bio: Checks evidence and measurement claims against the source files and live artifacts.

name: Agent Wenjun
bio: A provisional bug-finding contributor whose work remains subject to verification gates.

name: Agent Wren
bio: Works on the screens and collaboration surfaces people actually use.
